findings.summary: Verified Gwynn May 20 report p.34: 'The engagement continued lor an hour and a half without intermission on either side,'. Citation added to VA001 recorded-result (locator p.34 as proposed).

Verified Ward June 1 p.492 (the 300 shots and 1,700 pounds follow 'after the several cannonades in which we have been engaged, amounting altogether in the two weeks we are commissioned to ten hours') and Braine's May 22 statement in the Navy Volume 5 OCR (Freeborn came along, Commander Ward came on board, 'some twelve or fourteen shots'). VA002 ammunition-and-supplies value replaced as proposed; citation added; rationale appended with one change: Braine's statement gives no date, so the reviewer's 'on May 18' was omitted ('records the Thomas Freeborn under Ward firing on the unfinished battery above Sewell's Point, without giving a date, so the total may include VA001'). Memo Aquia bullet notes the cumulative figure.
Verified Magruder June 12 p.92: 'I have now to report that eighteen dead were found on the field,'. Citation added to VA003 casualty-records.

Verified Rosecrans Aug 28 p.118: 'General reports give Lee and Loring 10,000 men at Huntersville. Troops sickly.' WV004 ferry-sickness-trains second sentence replaced as proposed; the 'Troops sickly.' quote replaced by the two-sentence quote.

Verified: first telegram places Floyd (five regiments, three guns) at Cross-Lanes and 'AVise, with about the same force, on New River.'; the 5,000-10,000 estimate follows 'Has orders in full to hold his position at Gauley. Thinks he can do it.' in the second telegram. WV004 reported-force-scope value replaced as proposed (drops 'whole' before 'advance guard', matching Wise's quote), rationale sentence appended, p.118 citation added; the estimate clause deleted from reports-and-surprise. Western Virginia memo Cross-Lanes strength bullet corrected.

Verified Patterson July 3 (p.157: 3,500 scattered; 'again retreated to a point seven miles from here, where they have been re-enforced by a party under Colonel Bee, claimed in all to be thirty thousand ; in reality, thirteen thousand') and July 4 telegram (15,000-18,000 foot, 22 guns, 650 horse). WV002 reported-force-scope last sentence replaced as proposed; rationale sentence appended; p.157 citation for the Bee clause added. Manassas memo Patterson bullet updated.

Verified Stringham Sept 2 letter encloses 'a correct list* of the prisoners captured' with the compilers' 'List omitted. It contained 670 names.'; nothing establishes the frozen 770's basis. NC001 casualty-records rationale sentence replaced with the reviewer's text.

Verified and accepted but not applied here: c298447 adds 81 records, of which 78 are the 1861 passes' (the other three are Carolinas successors); its 33 new selections are 3 Carolinas successors, 3 Nicolay and 27 report selections. docs/sources.md is the primary's document and outside this reconciliation's scope; the primary should replace '- thirty report selections.' with '- twenty-seven report selections (thirty selections in all, with Nicolay's three).' Each memo records this; per-pass record counts (8+18+27+11+6+8=78) are unchanged.
SC001 fort-and-batteries: 'built of brick upon an artificial island' cited (p.62).

SC001: provisions-and-powder adds Nicolay's fifty barrels taken from the magazine and all but five rolled into the sea by Anderson's order (pp.67-68, two citations); notice-and-demand adds Anderson's reply that he would evacuate by noon on April 15 unless he received controlling instructions or supplies, and the 3:20 a.m. one-hour notice (p.61, three citations).

VA001 open_questions: Braine's May 22 statement (p.645, read not selected) places Commander Ward (listed VA002 commander) and the Thomas Freeborn firing twelve or fourteen shots at the unfinished battery; it gives no date and Gwynn's 'steam-tug' is not identified with the Freeborn. The 'recorded only in Gwynn's account' sentence now says 'among the selected sources'.

Verified the timings (Ward May 31 two hours then nearly an hour; Ruggles May 31 about 10 a.m. to about 1 p.m.; Ward June 1 11:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; Ruggles June 1 about 9 a.m.-4 p.m.). VA002 recorded-result rationale records the unreconciled timings; seven citations added. Memo Aquia bullet notes the timing difference.

VA003: 'fired on in the dark' (not in Pierce) replaced by Pierce's volley from the armed men and Townsend's regiment's indiscriminate fire (two p.84 citations); 'two fresh regiments' replaced by Allen's First New York in the lane and Carr's Second in line over the Fifth's ground (three p.85 citations, including 'Shortly after I directed all the forces to retire.').

WV003: recorded-result cites Nicolay's 'the Unionists had such advantage in numbers that the contest was quickly decided.' (p.149); casualty-records marks the 135 burials as Nicolay's paraphrase ('He also places') and its rationale records Nicolay's 560 men/33 officers against Pegram's 525 (359+166)/30 (22+8), not reconciled. Memo results bullet adds the surrender-count difference.
WV004 floyd-and-cox: 'draw his forces' -> 'draw Wise's own forces' (Wise's quote reads 'my forces').

Verified Rust's report is addressed 'General Loring, Commanding'. WV005 prisoners-and-spies: 'knew of Lee's movements' -> 'knew of the movements of Loring's column (Rust's addressee)'; the addressee line cited (p.192).
VA004 reported-force-scope: Nicolay's 'three regi- ments of Longstreet's brigade, which bore the first assault,' cited (p.179) and noted in the rationale; Manassas memo dispute bullet updated.

VA005: reported-force-scope rationale says Nicolay's 32,073 includes Kirby Smith's, Fisher's and Hill's troops arriving between noon and four o'clock (p.176 citation); casualty-records value adds McDowell's 'much under the true number' qualifier (p.322 citation) and the rationale says Nicolay's Union 481/1,011 repeat McDowell's return (19+462; 64+947), dependence not corroboration. Manassas memo updated.

Verified Martin p.141: 'The report of Commodore Barron and Major Andrews of the action of the 29th contains all that is material'. NC001 open_questions records that the report was read but not selected, so the Confederate side of the capitulation rests on the articles and Martin's clipping-copied report.

The reviewer asks for the Beauregard dependency-note fix only if a metadata-only revision is made for another reason; this reconciliation registers no successor, so or2-beauregard-blackburns-ford-selections-v1 stays as registered. Recorded in the Manassas memo.

Null dates for Nicolay's title-and-preface, McDowell's 'August 4', Beauregard's 'August —, 1861' and Stringham's two-date section are allowed and kept; they could be filled after a print check. The T. J. Jackson record's 'in this worktree' phrasing stays in the immutable record. Recorded in the Charleston, Manassas and Carolina coast memos.

Verified Morris p.67: 'From the reports of Colonel Dumont ... much difficulty in an accurate statement of the enemy's losses.' WV001 casualty-records value says the fifteen to forty Confederate killed are from Dumont's reports; one citation.

Recorded in the recorded-result rationales with eight citations: WV006 Rosecrans three hours vs Floyd nearly four; WV007 Reynolds four hours under fire vs H. R. Jackson's Oct 3 dispatch (attack at 8 o'clock, four and a half hours of fire) and Oct 7 report (7 a.m. to 2.30 p.m.) - the review's 'Jackson says 4½ hours, from 7 to 2:30' joins two statements, which are recorded separately; WV008 Jones about three hours vs Johnson 7.15 a.m. to 1.45 p.m. Western Virginia memo results bullet updated.
